Dated this the 8th day of April, 2025 The petitioner in O.P.(M.V.) No. 1569/2007 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Perumbavoor, is the appellant herein.
(For the purpose of convenience, the parties are hereafter referred to as per their rank before the Tribunal).
2. The petitioner filed the above O.P. under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation for the injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 27.04.2007.

According to the petitioner, on 27.04.2007 at about 9.30 a.m., while he was driving a car along the Aluva-Perumbavoor road, a mini lorry bearing Reg.No. KL-10-M-3216 driven by the 2nd respondent in a rash and negligent manner, hit on the car and as a result of the accident, the petitioner sustained serious injuries.
3. The 1st respondent is the owner, the 2nd respondent is the driver and 3rd respondent is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
According to the petitioner, the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.

The quantum of compensation claimed in the O.P.
is Rs.6,86,000/-(limited to 3,00,000/-).
4. The insurance company filed a written statement, admitting the 2025:KER:32931 accident as well as policy, but disputing the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.

5. The evidence in the case consists of the documentary evidence Exts.A1 to A10, X1 and B1.
6.

After evaluating the evidence on record, the Tribunal found negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, awarded a total compensation of Rs.1,84,327/- and directed the insurer to pay the same.
7. Aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the petitioner preferred this appeal.

8. Now the point that arises for consideration is the following:
Whether the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable?

sentences.text: 10. The Point: In this case the accident as well as valid insurance policy of the offending vehicle are admitted.
One of the contentions raised by the learned counsel for the petitioner is regarding the income of the petitioner as fixed by the Tribunal.
As per the claim petition, the petitioner was working 2025:KER:32931 as Teacher in a C.B.S.E. school, Aluva, earning Rs.6,322/- per month, but the Tribunal fixed his monthly income at Rs.3500/-.
The learned counsel for the insurer would argue that the income fixed by the tribunal is reasonable.

11. The learned counsel for the petitioner relied upon Ext.A9 salary certificate issued by the principal of the school, stating that, she was working as teacher in that C.B.S.E School and getting a monthly salary of Rs.6,322/-.
PW1 was also examined to prove the same.

As per the dictum laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236], the notional income of a coolie, in the year 2007 will come to Rs.6000/-.

entities.text: Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In the above circumstances, I do not find any grounds to disbelieve Ext.A9 and as such the monthly income of the petitioner is fixed at Rs. 6,322/-.
12.

In the accident the petitioner sustained the following injuries:
1. Lacerated wound on the left frontal region 6 x 1 cm,
2. Lacerated wound on the left side of front of neck and 3. Contused abrasions on the extremities.

Ext. A7, discharge summary shows that, he had lacerated wound over left forehead and frontal region, multiple small lacerated wounds over left side of the face, cheek and forehead, left back eye, lacerated wound over anterior lower and left lateral back, multiple abrasions over 2025:KER:32931 face and extremities.
C.T.Scan of brain showed Left ZM complex fracture."
13. As per Exhibit X1 disability certificate, the petitioner suffered 10% permanent physical disability.
It was issued by the medical board.
The Tribunal, has accepted the permanent physical disability of the petitioner as such and hence, I do not find any grounds to disbelieve the same.
Therefore, the permanent physical disability of the petitioner is accepted as 10%, as fixed by the Tribunal.
14. On the date of accident, the petitioner was aged 35 years.

Therefore, 40% of the monthly income is to be added towards future prospects, as held in the decision in National Insurance Co. Ltd v.
Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680] and the multiplier to be applied is 16, as held in Sarla Verma v.
Delhi Transport Corporation, [(2009) 6 SCC 121].

In the above circumstances, the loss of disability will come to Rs.1,69,935/-.
15.
According to the learned counsel for the petitioner, because of the injuries sustained in the accident, the petitioner had to take leave for a period of 14 months from the school.
In order to substantiate the same contention, he has relied upon Ext.A10.

In Ext.A10, a certificate issued by the Manju vs Manoharan on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145332183/
3 2025:KER:32931 Principal, Christava Mahilayalam Pubic School, it is stated that the petitioner was only on leave from 01.06.2005 to 31.03.2007 and it is also stated that because of the injuries sustained in the accident, the petitioner could not continue her job as a teacher in the school.

sentences.text: However, PW1 deposed that the petitioner resigned at her own will.
16. In Ext.A10 it is stated that, because of the injuries sustained in the accident, the petitioner had availed leave for the period from 01.06.2005 to 31.03.2007.
However, the petitioner was treated as an inpatient only for a period of 18 days.
PW1 was not the person who issued Ext.A10.

There is no reliable evidence to prove that she was on leave for the period from 01.06.2005 to 31.03.2007,
because of the injuries sustained in the accident.
17. Towards loss of earning, the tribunal has awarded only Rs.10,500/-being the income for 3 months @ Rs.3500/-.

However, considering the facts, including the nature of the injuries sustained in the accident, I hold that, she might have no lost income because of the injuries sustained in the accident, at least for a period of 9 months.
Therefore, towards 'loss of income' the petitioner is entitled to get a sum of Rs. 56,898/- (6,322 x 9 months).
Towards the head 'pain and sufferings', the Tribunal has awarded Rs.22,000/-.
Towards 'loss of amenities of life' Rs.13,000/- was awarded and towards 'extra nourishment' Rs.2,250/- was awarded.
According to the learned counsel for the petitioner, the compensation awarded on those heads are on the lower side.
19. The petitioner sustained serious injuries in the accident and was treated as inpatient for 18 days.

Because of the injuries sustained, the percentage of disability suffered and the length of treatment undergone by the petitioner, I hold that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal on the heads 'pain and sufferings', 'loss of amenities of life' and 'extra nourishment' are on the lower side and hence they are enhanced to Rs.60,000/-, 40,000/- and 5,000/- respectively.
20.
No change is required, in the amounts awarded on other heads, as the compensation awarded on those heads appears to be just and reasonable.
21. Therefore, the petitioner/appellant is entitled to get a total compensation of Rs.4,05,370/-, as modified and recalculated above and given in the table below, for easy reference:

In the result, this Appeal is allowed in part, and 3rd respondent is directed to deposit a total sum of Rs.4,05,370/- (Rupees Four lakhs five thousand three hundred and seventy only), less the amount already deposited, if any, along with interest @
8% per annum , from the date of the petition till deposit/realisation, with proportionate costs, within a period of two months from today.
23. On depositing the aforesaid amount, the Tribunal shall disburse the entire amount to the petitioner, excluding court fee payable, if any, without delay, as per rules.
24. The Tribunal found that the 2nd respondent had no valid driving 2025:KER:32931 licence at the time of the accident and also that the mini lorry had no permit at the relevant time.
Therefore the Tribunal has permitted the 3rd respondent to recover the compensation from respondents 1 and 2.
Before this Court also the respondents 1 and 2 did not turn up and as such I do not find any grounds to interfere with above finding of the Tribunal.
In other words, the permission granted to the 3rd respondent to recover the compensation from respondents 1 and 2 is retained.

Sd/-
